source_review.notes: Reviewed current Google Benchmark, OpenJDK JMH, pyperf, Go testing, Criterion.rs, Linux perf-security, SPEC CPU 2026, and NIST documentation plus the primary Kalibera/Jones, Georges/Buytaert/Eeckhout, and Mytkowicz et al. methodology publications. All eleven final destinations returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Checked workload/environment/implementation/measurement notation, hierarchy indices, estimand definitions, paired ratios, and lower-is-better direction.
Separated observation, inner iteration, repetition, process, session/environment, effect size, confidence interval, and practical threshold.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Candidate/baseline and baseline/candidate ratios are explicitly named and never interchanged.

evidence: Recomputed baseline total 808 and mean 101.000 ns; candidate total 736 and mean 92.000 ns.
Recomputed candidate/baseline ratio 92/101=0.910891... and reciprocal speedup 101/92=1.097826..., rounding to 0.911 and 1.098.
Checked all eight paired candidate observations are lower than their corresponding baseline observations.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The table is deliberately synthetic and carries no runtime-performance or uncertainty claim.

evidence: Re-derived reciprocal relation s=1/q for q=C/B and s=B/C under positive timings.
Checked the hierarchical decomposition assigns environment, process, repetition, and within-repetition variation to distinct indexed levels.
Re-derived that batching reduces relative timer overhead but does not create independent process or machine replications.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Ratio of means, mean of paired ratios, and ratio of medians are explicitly treated as different estimands.

evidence: Reviewed empty/small/large, capacity and resize thresholds, load factor, tombstones, skew/collisions, key cost, hit ratio, state/history, cold/warm/transition, and failure/teardown regimes.

Reviewed timer resolution, dead-code elimination, constant folding, hoisting, batching, setup asymmetry, JIT/deoptimization, GC, allocator, ASLR, paging, NUMA, affinity, thermal/frequency state, background load, and virtualization.

Reviewed outliers, exclusions, pseudoreplication, multiplicity, inconclusive intervals, tail sampling, open/closed-loop load, coordinated omission, counter multiplexing, infrastructure retries, hostile input, and clinical limits.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: No relative performance ordering or rough ratio is treated as a cross-hardware invariant.

evidence: Equivalent abstract work and correctness are checked before timing; setup, validation, and cleanup inclusion are declared.
Baseline and candidate receive the same declared workload under recorded randomized/counterbalanced blocks, and output consumption protects intended work.
Raw observations, hierarchy, failures, exclusions, versions, flags, order, and environment stay attached to every claim.
invariant_checking.notes: Inference is limited to sampled workloads, sizes, environments, runtime states, and experimental units.

evidence: Reviewed equivalent-work and timing-region obligations as prerequisites to a comparative effect.
Reviewed pairing/blocking argument against comparable block conditions, carryover control, and preserved pair identities.
Reviewed why finite empirical curves cannot prove asymptotic bounds and why counter correlation alone cannot prove a causal mechanism.
proof_review.notes: The chapter offers experimental argument structure, not a proof of any benchmark result or hardware mechanism.

evidence: The hierarchy and pairing discussions state design assumptions and constrain the population of inference.
Concurrent and clinical examples require correctness, systems, domain, safety, privacy, quality, human-factors, operations, and regulatory review without claiming it occurred.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Benchmark observations are not represented as intrinsic structure properties, safety evidence, or deployment authorization.

evidence: The Python analysis snippet passed exact seven-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the recorded toolchain.
It emits evidence=synthetic_analysis_not_runtime_benchmark; all eleven source destinations and local links were directly checked.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No real data structure, benchmark harness, compiler optimization, runtime warm-up, hardware counter, memory, energy, concurrency, or clinical system was measured.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed claim/estimand design, benchmark levels, correctness, timed units, batching, optimization barriers, workload dimensions, size regimes, amortized tails, environment, warm-up, hierarchical repetition, ordering/blocking, statistics, ratios, metric distinctions, counters, concurrent load, regression governance, evidence packages, and scope limits.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed operation equivalence, setup/teardown boundaries, input streams, output consumption, harness calibration, process forks, controlled workers, affinity/NUMA/power/thermal metadata, raw artifacts, predeclared exclusions and thresholds, confirmatory reruns, allocation/profile separation, overload accounting, and PR/release use.

pedagogical_review.notes: Completes the first DSE block by connecting contracts and cost models to disciplined evidence, corrects unsafe invariance claims found in legacy material, uses one deterministic synthetic analysis without pretending it benchmarks runtime, counters sixteen misconceptions, and supplies ten examples plus five matched exercises and answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external statistics, benchmarking-tool, compiler/runtime, operating-system, architecture, performance, concurrency, security, reliability, medical, clinical, safety, privacy, regulatory, quality, accessibility, human-factors, operations, or independent review is claimed. The chapter and synthetic analysis prove neither real performance, representativeness, causal mechanism, portability, regression absence, capacity, patient safety, certification, nor deployment fitness.
